newsitem.title: UK: British and German stocks briefly hit highs.
newsitem.headline: British and German stocks briefly hit highs.

text.p: Stocks in London and Frankfurt soared briefly to new highs in early trading on Tuesday powered by another record close in New York as hopes grew that U.S. interest rates would remain unchanged.
The bull market stampede in Wall Street overnight drove up London's FTSE 100 index to a trading peak of 3,986.7 points before slipping back slightly by mid-morning as investors had second thoughts.
Traders said the market, despite a string of healthy corporate results, had reached a psychological crossroads as investors speculated what lay beyond the key 4,000 point level.
"The problem is, we've reached the edge of the map and people are sitting down to think, what next?", one dealer said.

In Frankfurt, trading on the computerised IBIS index touched 2639.07 points in opening deals, eclipsing the previous trading best of 2632.51 before also slipping back. Floor trading which closed at a record high on Monday was down a few points.

Behind Europe's opening surges was New York's record-breaking run on Monday. The Dow Jones industrial average poked through 5,900 points for the first time just one session after cracking the 5,800 level on hopes that the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates unchanged.
"It's pretty amazing. It's got 6,000 written all over it," said Jim Benning, a trader at BT Brokerage of Wall Street's performance.
But some investors in London had their doubts about the stamina of New York's gains and held back. Traders said there was evidence that funds were sitting on "piles of cash".

"There is some feeling of disbelief about Wall Street and we haven't matched it move for move. Given the strength of UK corporate results, we should have few problems pushing higher but the commitment is lacking," a dealer said.
Dealers said volumes in early dealings were small and quoted this as evidence of the anxieties gnawing at investors.
Dealers said the market's focus may be shifting to domestic politics as investors weigh up the prospects of a future Labour government on business policies.

In Frankfurt too, the push to higher levels ran out of steam with traders switching attention from Wall Street to upcoming German economic data including a consumer confidence survey expected on Thursday and rumoured to be strong.
French stocks opened slightly higher before also heading lower on consolidation following Monday's gains.
In Milan, shares in crisis-struck Italian information technology group Olivetti fell 10 percent, triggering automatic suspension 20 minutes after the start of trade.

The stock plummeted to a fresh record low of 465 lire per share after news market regulator Consob demanded answers on the group's financial performance. The dollar began the European day virtually unchanged from Monday's closing levels and looked set for another quiet session.
U.S. industrial production figures due later on Tuesday would command attention and were regarded as likely to keep the interest rate discussion lively.
Industrial production is expected to have risen about 0.4 percent in August after a 0.1 percent increase in July. Healthy figures would rekindle speculation of a tightening in interest rates.
CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5110 marks and 110.14 yen compared with late Monday's 1.5105 marks and 110.13 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0900 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 4.3 at 3,972.9.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 2.66 points at 2,083.53.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index was down 3.51 points at 2,626.36.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was quoted higher at $383.45 compared with $382.70 at the London close on Monday. Silver was at $5.07, up two cents.
